title: Vyomanaut V2 — Microservice + Provider Daemon Fleet (NFR-025/026)
description: NFR-025's eight mandatory microservice metrics, exact names per internal/metrics/microservice.go (OBS.1.1/OBS.1.2), PLUS a second row (added, M18 Stage 3 rig) covering the seven NFR-026 provider-daemon metrics from internal/metrics/daemon.go. [Correction, round 2] The patch that added the daemon row also said the microservice side (the first nine panels) "still shows no data on the Stage 3 rig — cmd/microservice still registers no /metrics handler at all." That was wrong, checked too narrowly: a separate, already-built, already-tested path exists at internal/api/router.go (GET /metrics mounted directly on the microservice's own API listener, gated behind RouterConfig.ExposePrometheusMetrics / cmd/microservice's --expose-metrics flag / VYOMANAUT_EXPOSE_METRICS=1, off by default — internal/api/router_test.go's TestPrometheusMetricsRouteIsOptIn pins exactly this). Turn that flag on (scripts/demo/up.sh --expose-metrics), add the coordinator's own address to deployments/observability/targets/microservice.json, and these first nine panels receive real data — the metrics were being updated on every run all along; nothing was ever exposing them until that flag exists. internal/metrics/microservice.go's own StartMicroserviceMetricsServer / ShutdownMicroserviceMetricsServer remain genuinely unused after this correction: a second, separate-port mechanism for the same metrics that the router-mounted approach appears to have superseded. Worth a decision (document the two as intentionally serving different tracks, or drop the unused one) rather than something resolved here.

panels.title: Audit challenges issued
panels.description: Challenge throughput (vyomanaut_audit_challenges_issued_total).

panels.title: Audit results by outcome
panels.description: Network reliability, split PASS/FAIL/TIMEOUT (vyomanaut_audit_results_total).

panels.title: Audit TIMEOUT rate (1h)
panels.description: NFR-027 AuditTimeoutRateHigh signal — alert fires above 0.05. [Corrected, Grafana panel fix / evening-run review] The previous expression divided rate(...{result="TIMEOUT"}) by the bare, unaggregated rate(vyomanaut_audit_results_total[1h]) — that denominator is actually THREE separate series (one per result label: PASS, FAIL, TIMEOUT), not one combined total, since AuditResultsTotal is a CounterVec keyed on `result` (internal/metrics/microservice.go) and rate() does not sum across label values on its own. PromQL's default one-to-one vector matching then paired the numerator's TIMEOUT series with the denominator's identically-labeled TIMEOUT series and quietly dropped the unmatched PASS/FAIL series — so the panel always read exactly 100%, even during the morning run where the unaggregated 'Audit results by outcome' panel showed timeouts were a small fraction of the total. sum() on both sides collapses each side to the single intended series first.

panels.title: Provider score distribution
panels.description: Distribution of computed provider reliability scores (vyomanaut_scoring_provider_score).

panels.title: Repair queue depth
panels.description: NFR-027 RepairQueueDepthHigh signal — alert fires above 1,000.

panels.title: Repair jobs completed
panels.description: Repair throughput (vyomanaut_repair_jobs_completed_total).

panels.title: Escrow events by type
panels.description: Payment volume, split DEPOSIT/RELEASE/SEIZURE/REVERSAL (vyomanaut_payment_escrow_events_total).

panels.title: Microservice replica count
panels.description: NFR-027 MicroserviceReplicasDegraded signal — alert fires when healthy < 3.

panels.title: Foreground DB read p99 (windowed)
panels.description: Dashboard view of the ADR-033 cumulative histogram (vyomanaut_db_read_latency_seconds). NFR-028's actual background-throttle decision reads the process-local 60s sliding window (metrics.ForegroundReadP99Window in internal/metrics/window.go), not this PromQL quantile — the two will diverge under a very recent burst, by design.

panels.title: Daemon: chunks stored (per desk)
panels.description: [Added, M18 Stage 3] Chunk-store activity per provider (vyomanaut_daemon_chunks_stored_total). Cumulative counter, so this is a rate — a flat line at zero on a desk that should be receiving vetting/repair traffic is the first sign something upstream stopped routing work to it. Requires that desk's provider to have been started with --metrics-addr=0.0.0.0:9091 / -MetricsAddr 0.0.0.0:9091; a desk missing from the legend entirely usually means that flag was left off, not that the metric is broken.

panels.title: Daemon: audit responses sent (per desk)
panels.description: [Added, M18 Stage 3] Per-provider audit-response throughput (vyomanaut_daemon_audit_responses_sent_total). Cross-check against the microservice-side 'Audit results by outcome' panel above: if that panel's TIMEOUT share is climbing but every desk here still shows a healthy response rate, the timeouts are more likely network/relay-side than the provider failing to respond at all.

panels.title: Daemon: audit response latency p95 (per desk)
panels.description: [Added, M18 Stage 3] p95 of vyomanaut_daemon_audit_response_latency_milliseconds. [Note] Registered in milliseconds, not seconds — internal/metrics/daemon.go's own OBS.2.1 comment documents this as a deliberate exception to NFR-046's _seconds convention, kept because this histogram also feeds FR-029's human-facing CLI status view. The single slowest desk here is usually your bottleneck for the whole network's audit cycle time, not the average.

panels.title: Daemon: vLog append latency p95 (per desk)
panels.description: [Added, M18 Stage 3] p95 of vyomanaut_daemon_vlog_append_latency_milliseconds — local disk write performance per machine. Also milliseconds, same NFR-046 exception as the panel above. A desk that drifts upward here over a long run, while every other desk stays flat, points at that specific machine's disk (fragmentation, thermal throttling, a background scan) rather than anything in this project's own code.

panels.title: Daemon: content hash failures (per desk)
panels.description: [Added, M18 Stage 3] increase() of vyomanaut_daemon_content_hash_failures_total over 1h — the same metric alerts.yaml's ContentHashFailureDetected rule watches. This should sit at exactly zero for every desk, always. Any nonzero value is a real silent-corruption event on that machine's disk (architecture.md §23: trigger an accelerated re-audit of everything that provider holds), not noise to average away — hence the threshold coloring rather than a smoothed rate.

panels.title: Daemon: heartbeats sent (per desk)
panels.description: [Added, M18 Stage 3] rate() of vyomanaut_daemon_heartbeat_sent_total — each desk's connectivity signal. A line that flatlines here is usually visible minutes before the operator console's own Provider fleet panel marks that machine OVERDUE/DEPARTED (departure-threshold is on the order of minutes; the flatline itself starts at the missed heartbeat), so this is the earliest warning of a machine that has gone to sleep or lost its ZeroTier link.

panels.title: Daemon: RAM constrained (per desk)
panels.description: [Added, M18 Stage 3] vyomanaut_daemon_ram_constrained — 1 while that desk is under RAM pressure (Session 13.6.1, A1), 0 otherwise. Expect a flat 0 for every desk on typical lab hardware; a desk pinned at 1 is worth checking directly (Task Manager / Activity Monitor) before trusting its other numbers on this dashboard, since a RAM-constrained daemon is more likely to also be the one posting slow audit/vLog latency above.

panels.title: Repair job duration (p50 / p95)
panels.description: [Added, Stage 3 final test] End-to-end wall-clock time per repair job — created_at to completed_at, queue wait plus execution, from vyomanaut_repair_job_duration_seconds (internal/repair/queue.go's MarkJobComplete). Coordinator-side and singular in this demo (no `desk` label — there is one coordinator), unlike the per-desk daemon histograms above. The morning run's repair cycle had to be read off two separate 'Repair queue depth' screenshots and eyeballed at roughly 8-9 minutes for a 132-job backlog; this panel gives the real per-job number directly. A job that never completes (as in the evening run, where nothing was ever real enough to repair from) produces no observation at all here rather than a misleadingly low one — absence of data on this panel during an active incident is itself informative.

panels.title: Assignment vs confirmed delivery (fleet, per second)
panels.description: Stage 3 final report Sec 6.1 - coordinator bookkeeping rate (vyomanaut_storage_chunk_assignments_total, internal/api/upload.go assignSegment, incremented once per chunk_assignments row after commit) against the fleet's confirmed-store rate (vyomanaut_daemon_chunks_stored_total, cmd/provider/handler_upload.go line 337). A gap here is the assignment/delivery lag the chunk-count screenshot could only describe in prose. [Caveat] chunks_stored_total also fires for synthetic vetting chunks and repair-driven shard placements (DM Sec4.5 - the provider daemon cannot tell them apart from a real upload), so only trust this comparison during an upload window with the fleet fully ACTIVE and no repair backlog draining (see 'Repair queue depth').

panels.title: Cumulative assignment/delivery gap (shards)
panels.description: Running difference between total chunk_assignments rows committed and total confirmed provider stores, over the dashboard's own time range ($__range). A gap that returns to zero after an upload means delivery caught up; a gap that stays open is the finding, quantified in shards. Same vetting/repair conflation caveat as 'Assignment vs confirmed delivery' above applies to the second term.

panels.title: Audit PASS rate (5m)
panels.description: Stage 3 final report Sec 5.4's headline number, direct from the dashboard instead of computed by hand off the 'Audit results by outcome' graph. sum() on both numerator and denominator, same as the TIMEOUT-rate panel's own fix above: vyomanaut_audit_results_total is a CounterVec keyed on result (PASS|FAIL|TIMEOUT), and skipping sum() pairs each label with only its identically-labeled twin, silently dropping the other two.

panels.title: Audit FAIL rate (5m)
panels.description: Companion to 'Audit PASS rate (5m)' and the existing 'Audit TIMEOUT rate (1h)' panel: with all three on the same 0-1 scale, PASS + FAIL + TIMEOUT visibly sums to 1 and the reader can see the accounting closes. Same sum()-on-both-sides construction as the PASS panel, for the same reason.
